decision_audit_trail.rationale: Cross-source license classification contradiction: PyPI classifiers, ClearlyDefined, and artifact license text (typing_extensions-4.12.2.dist-info/LICENSE, PSF-2.0) confirm standard license, while downstream indexer classifies it as non-standard. Because authoring field omission vs parser fault cannot be definitively proven, unilateral parser blame assertion is removed.

dependency_relations.nature: Downstream ingestion of upstream registry metadata; consistency represents ingestion propagation, NOT independent ground-truth verification.
dependency_relations.subject: deps_dev

verdict.avoided_false_positive: Avoided discarding or flagging a legitimate package as license-incompatible while avoiding unverified attribution of parser fault.
verdict.details: deps.dev reports licenses: ['non-standard']. In contrast, PyPI registry classifiers contain '['License :: OSI Approved :: Python Software Foundation License']' and ClearlyDefined confirms 'Python-2.0.1'. The artifact typing_extensions-4.12.2.dist-info/LICENSE contains verified license text (PSF-2.0). Because upstream core metadata omits an explicit PEP 639 License-Expression header, authoring field omission versus downstream classifier parsing fault cannot be separated. Enforcing hard constraint: deleted DOWNSTREAM_PARSING_ERROR and removed unilateral parser responsibility assertion; recorded verifiable metadata contradiction.
verdict.summary: Downstream index license classification contradicts upstream and curated standards
